title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 7° of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' manuscript. Grothendieck is studying a group M_{ρ,σ} attached to two 'types' ρ, σ. It plausibly comes from the Lego/Teichmüller setting of the Longue Marche: ρ, σ might be orders of cyclic stabilisers, as in PSL2(Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3, with G_{ρ,σ} the ambient group, N_ρ and N_σ normalisers of the corresponding cyclic subgroups, and Z_{ρ,σ} a central or centraliser-type subgroup. Each of Z, N_ρ, N_σ, G carries a homomorphism δ to a common quotient γ_{ρ,σ}.

(100) He forms the 4-fold fibre product SoM^♮ = Z ×_γ N_ρ^♮ ×_γ N_σ^♮ ×_γ G^♮. Its elements are quadruples x = (u, a, b, U) with δ_Z(u) = δ_ρ(a) = δ_σ(b) = δ_G(U).

(101)-(102) There are three inclusions i_Z: Z → G, i_ρ: N_ρ → G and i_σ: N_σ → G, compatible with the δ's. Using them he defines three subgroups as graphs, cut out by the conditions U = i_Z(u), U = i_ρ(a) and U = i_σ(b) respectively. In each, U is determined by the other coordinates. So the projection forgetting U, from SoM onto SoΓ_{ρ,σ} := Z ×_γ N_ρ ×_γ N_σ, restricts to an isomorphism on each subgroup. In the exact sequence (52), 1 → G^+ → SoM → SoΓ → 1, the three subgroups are therefore splittings ('sous-groupes sections'), each isomorphic to SoΓ.

(103) He then pushes these along the canonical quotient SoM → M_{ρ,σ}, which presumably forgets or divides out the Z-coordinate. This defines M[0], M(ρ) and M(σ). The page also gives the alternative names M(1/2) and M(-ρ̄), suggesting a parametrisation of the three distinguished points by 0, 1/2 and -ρ̄.

Next page: explicitly, M[0] = {U ∈ Z}, M(ρ) = {U = a} and M(σ) = {U = b}. One gets semidirect decompositions M ≅ M(ρ)·𝔖^+ ≅ M(σ)·𝔖^+. M[0] is identified with the extension SoΓ of Γ by L_0, the pull-back of the extension Z.

Purpose: to have explicit section subgroups needed to analyse which (ρ,σ)-morphisms are 'admissible', i.e. satisfy the loop relation (96)/(99), first in the universal case.
errors: The graphs are subgroups only if each i_• is a homomorphism compatible with the δ maps, i.e. δ_G∘i_Z = δ_Z, etc. This is implicit and presumably established earlier.
The sentence 'Ces trois groupes sont manifestement tous trois isomorphes : Z×N_ρ×N_σ ≃ SoΓ' is elliptic. The intended meaning is that each is isomorphic to SoΓ via projection.

ideas.what: Fibre product of the centraliser/normaliser groups over a common quotient, forming SoM_{ρ,σ}
ideas.modern_name: iterated fibre product of groups over a base, i.e. a group over γ
ideas.where_published: not in Esquisse or Longue Marche as such, to my knowledge

ideas.what: Three graph subgroups U = i_Z(u), i_ρ(a), i_σ(b) giving three splittings of 1→G^+→SoM→SoΓ→1, and their images M[0], M(ρ), M(σ) in M_{ρ,σ}
ideas.modern_name: sections of a split extension / semidirect product decompositions attached to distinguished fixed points (cusp and orbifold points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard group theory; the specific objects are Grothendieck's in this manuscript

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping inside an unpublished framework: graph subgroups as sections of a split extension. The broader manuscript on the loop equation is unpublished, but nothing on this page is a substantive new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: 'on utilisant maintenant' should be 'en utilisant maintenant'.
The marginal note likely reads 'Les groupes M_{ρ,σ}[0], M_{ρ,σ}(ρ), M_{ρ,σ}(σ)'. The first bracket appears to be [0] (overwritten), not [ρ].
The top page number appears as '642' with an earlier number crossed out, rather than '692'. This reading is uncertain.
The superscript written ♮ is the same decoration rendered § on the next page; it should be transcribed consistently.
The kernel in the exact sequence (52) is a script/fraktur G^+ (𝔊^+, matching 𝔖^+ on the next page), not plain G^+.
